title: Latency Sentinel — quick reference & handoff scratch
content:
Purpose: quick mental model and minimal actions for the night person handling latency spikes. Not a full runbook — just what I want in my pocket during handoff.

Context / quick facts:
- Primary metric: p95 request latency across api.redwood/v1/generate (last 7d baseline ~ 420ms p95).
- Alert that usually matters: LATENCY-P95-CROSS-2-5m -> fires when p95 > 800ms for 5m.
- Secondary: GPU-queue-depth > 20 on dedicated pools; indicates batching or backpressure issue.
- Peak windows historically: 09:00-11:30 PT and 18:00-20:00 PT (watch for ramp-ups).

What I check first (order matters):
1) Dashboard quick scan (Grafana - SRE Home -> Latency Overview): p95, p99, request rate. Look for correlated increase in request rate or dropped tokens.
2) Ingress / API tier: check ALB 5xx rate (ALB/NGINX) and throttling errors. If 5xx + latency, route likely congested; consider scaling frontends.
3) GPU pools: open Dedicated console -> pool metrics. If queue depth > 20 and GPU utilization > 90% on most nodes -> likely serving-side saturation.
4) Model fallback events: check routing logs for automatic fallback to smaller model. If fallbacks occurred recently, note timestamp and reason.
5) Traces: sample a few slow traces via Honeycomb/Datadog traces. Look for where time is spent (decode loop? kv cache miss?).

Immediate mitigations (fast, reversible):
- If frontends overloaded (high 5xx + CPU): scale frontend ASG up by +2 instances (or trigger autoscale policy if manual). Note: scaling normally helps within 2–3 minutes.
- If GPU pool saturated: enable burst-capacity (if available) or flip routing to lower-cost / lower-latency region (Redwood Console -> routing -> fallback) — annotate in incident notes.
- Apply temporary rate limit reduction: reduce per-client rate by 20% as soft throttle to shed tail load. Command: run-tool throttle set --policy=global --pct=80 (confirm with on-call comms).
- If KV cache miss storm: purge a small prefix? Better: enable KV warmup for hottest prefixes using: infra-tool kv-prime --model=xxx --prefix="/v1/generate/hot" --duration=5m

When to escalate to eng-on-call (SRE escalation criteria):
- Latency persists >20 minutes after mitigations and p95 > 1s
- Data plane (GPU) has >25% node OOMs or repeated process restarts
- Evidence of model serving or runtime bug (OOM logs, kernel errors) — page on-call-eng and attach trace id + node ids

Useful commands & quick snippets (have in terminal snippets):
- Check queue depth aggregate: infra-cli pool metrics --pool=dedicated-prod --metric=queue_depth --window=5m
- Tail runtime errors: ssh node-123 'sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime -f --since "5 minutes ago"'
- Trigger fallback routing: redwoodctl routing set --policy=latency --fallback=smaller-llama2-7b --duration=10m
- Rollback last model rollout (if suspect): redwoodctl rollout revert --service=hosted-api --to=version-2026-02-02-rc1 --reason="latency spike correlate"

What to log in the handoff note (very short):
- time window observed, key metrics (p95/p99/request rate), what I tried, commands run, whether any escalations, who was paged, links to traces/dashboards.
- Example: \"2026-02-18 03:20–03:46 UTC: p95 1.1s -> frontends scaled +2 at 03:22, pool queue depth 32 -> enabled fallback (smaller-llama2-7b) at 03:24, spike resolved 03:34. Paged eng-oncall (Arjun) at 03:26. Traces: https://honeycomb.io/trace/abc123 / Dash: <grafana link>\"

Open questions / items to follow up (notes-to-self):
- Investigate KV cache efficiency for prefix /v1/generate/chat -- misses spike correlated with warm-up after deploys. Possible pre-warm strategy.
- Could circuit-breaker be more aggressive for tail latencies? Spike came from a handful of clients sending long-context sequences.
- Add a synthetic check to exercise the short-token path every 30s (helps keep KV hot).

Personal reminders for handoff convo:
- Keep it brief: 2 bullets of what I saw + 1 action I took. If unresolved, call out next steps and who to contact.
- If you had to flip config flags, mention exact flag names and duration. Avoid vague language.

Attachments / quick links (copy into Slack handoff):
- Grafana: <SRE Home - Latency Overview>
- Traces: paste the 2–3 trace ids I captured
- Incident Jira (if created): SRE-3842 (temp tracking)

Last 3 fast wins that worked in past:
- Short-term fallback to smaller model (resolved within 8–12m twice)
- Soft throttle per-client heavy IPs (shed 15–20% tail requests)
- Short cache warmup job for top prefixes (reduced p99 in follow-up period)

TODO (low effort for next run):
- Add a one-click Grafana panel with the 3 relevant metrics + link copy in Console (2h).
- Add short note in Confluence: "KV warmup play" with steps and owners (ask Arjun).

-- end of scratch. Keep this as portable text for handoff message.

Notes to self: leave terminal snippets in ~/.sre/snippets and sync with ops-dotfiles before shift. If you break anything, write it down in the incident comment — helps post-mortem.
